resolutions.title: An unclosed quote on a non-orbit shell line hides every later orbit line in the fence
resolutions.action: The tokenizer follows the shell's backslash rule (outside quotes the next character; inside double quotes ", \, $ and a backtick; inside single quotes nothing), and a quote still open at a shell fence's end fails extraction whatever the opening line's first token, so a line of another tool cannot hide the orbit lines after it. Ungating the failure surfaced a real mis-tokenized line on today's surface (external-handoff.md:151, the runner launch): its redirect `< '<run-dir>/…'` was read as a <…> placeholder that swallowed the quote; a `<` followed by whitespace is now a redirect. The sweep's figures are unchanged (129 parsed, 35 bare, 0 failures, 0 guard hits). Tests: both swallow cases in the places table, the backslash and redirect rules in the tokenizer, and two injections into a real reference fence; all five fail against the HEAD helper. The spec's quoted-argument row and tokenizer paragraph and design D3 state the rules.

resolutions.title: The accepted-codes rule rejects `orbit help <command>`, which the real CLI accepts with exit 0
resolutions.action: A thrown exit is accepted exactly when commander's exit code is 0, as the CLI's process exits: --help, --version and help <command>. ACCEPTED_EXIT_CODES is retired for acceptedExit(error). Measured on both the neutral parse and the real CLI: help status 0, help frobnicate 1, help 0, external 1, external save 1. The builder test accepts help status and rejects help frobnicate (it fails against the HEAD helper); the spec's exits row and the group scenario name the exit code, and design D2 says why the error code cannot decide.

resolutions.action: The places limit's residual kind names the double-backtick inline span and, inside a shell fence, a `$ ` or assignment prefix and a trailing-backslash continuation (a false failure); the residual method no longer claims the guard reads every line — it reads every line outside a shell fence — and names how the shell-fence members are found.

resolutions.title: The no-hook assertion cannot see the root hook's effect
resolutions.action: The no-hook test clears NO_COLOR, runs `--no-color list` with the rest, and asserts NO_COLOR is still unset, restoring any prior value. Shown able to fail: with the root hook registered regardless of the option, the test fails.

resolutions.title: The neutralisation closure leaves out requiredOption, which the CLI uses
resolutions.action: The neutralisation table gains a requiredOption row (external save's --as and --from: kept and enforced, a missing one rejecting with commander.missingMandatoryOptionValue), and the closure lists requiredOption. A re-grep of the CLI's register sources for every commander setting found only allowUnknownOption and requiredOption beyond the table's rows. The builder test asserts the rejection and the accepted full form.

final_assessment: Five of five resolved, all repairs: the tokenizer follows the shell's quoting and an open quote fails whatever line opened it (which surfaced and fixed a redirect read as a placeholder), acceptance is by exit code so help <command> parses, and three smaller repairs to the places limit, the no-hook test and the closure.
